why: At a=0.25 the general reliability part is fully present but only about a quarter of the dose-scaled math part, and the math part matters most on hard328's near-zero-p problems, so theta(0.25) recovers about 0.4 of the 164->206 gap, not the 0.66 it recovers on MATH-500.

The general part is saturated, so going from a=0.25 to 0.5 adds only the second quarter of the dose-scaled math part (about +6-7 problems on hard328), which leaves theta(0.5) well short of RL's 206, unlike the MATH-500 plateau.
Code-RL has the general reliability part but none of the math-specific part, so it fixes only the moderate-p problems and recovers about 0.3 of the 164->206 gap on hard328.
theta(0.5) carries only half of the math-specific dose that hard328's near-zero-p problems need, so it trails RL plain (206) by about 19 problems, about -6 points.
Code-RL lacks the math-specific part, so it misses roughly the 30 near-zero-p problems RL solves (about 176 vs 206), about -9 points.
Both models share the saturated general part, so they differ only by theta(0.5)'s half dose of the math-specific part, which is worth about 11 problems on hard328.
